# Spatial domains

In this section, we use [Novae](https://mics-lab.github.io/novae/) to identify spatial domains within this dataset.


```{r}
#| label: loading preamble
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

source("./preamble.R")
```

As this package is written in python, we start by generating an adata object from our filtered Seurat object.

```{r}
#| label: convert_seurat_anndata
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| eval: false


# if there's no seurat object, read it in
if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$seurat_file_postCellTyping)
}

# Convert to single cell experiment
sce <- as.SingleCellExperiment(seu.obj)

# Save as h5ad
h5ad_path <- paste0(objects_dir, "/assay_data.h5ad")
writeH5AD(sce, file = h5ad_path, X_name = "counts", assay = "counts")

```

Next, we switch into `Python` and run novae to generate spatial domains.

```{python}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true

import novae
import igraph
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scanpy as sc
import numpy as np
import os
import hdf5plugin

sc.settings.figdir = os.path.join(r.niche_dir, "Plots")
novae.settings.auto_preprocessing = True


# Read in sample
adata = sc.read_h5ad("analysis/Robjects/assay_data.h5ad")

## convert spatial from mm to microns for novae

# Extract coordinates from obs
x_mm = adata.obs["x_slide_mm"].to_numpy()
y_mm = adata.obs["y_slide_mm"].to_numpy()

# Create spatial_mm matrix
spatial_mm = np.column_stack((x_mm, y_mm))
adata.obsm["spatial_mm"] = spatial_mm

# Convert to microns
spatial_um = spatial_mm * 1000
adata.obsm["spatial_um"] = spatial_um

# Duplicate spatial_um to spatial
adata.obsm["spatial"] = spatial_um

## Start running novae
# Create a Delaunay graph of the data
novae.spatial_neighbors(adata, radius=80, coord_type='generic')

# Use a quick plot to ensure that neighbors were calculated appropriately
# Looking for very few red (unconnected) cells that are only on the edges of tissue
novae.plot.connectivities(adata)

# Load in pre-trained model
model1 = novae.Novae.from_pretrained("MICS-Lab/novae-human-0")

# Fine tune model based on CosMx data in this study
model1.fine_tune(adata, max_epochs=50, logger=True) 
model1.compute_representations(adata, zero_shot=False) 

for i in range(1, 20):
  model1.assign_domains(adata, i)

model1_dir = os.path.join(r.niche_dir, "novae_model_one")
model1.save_pretrained(save_directory=model1_dir)

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
dh = model1.plot_domains_hierarchy()
plt.savefig(os.path.join(r.niche_dir, "Plots", "novae_model1_hierarchy.png"))
plt.close()


adata.write_h5ad(
  os.path.join(r.objects_dir, "anndata-plus-novae.h5ad"),
  compression=hdf5plugin.FILTERS["zstd"],
  compression_opts=hdf5plugin.Zstd(clevel=5).filter_options
)



```

Hierarchy of the domains assigned by novae:
```{r}
knitr::include_graphics(paste0(niche_dir, "/Plots/novae_model1_hierarchy.png"))
```

Plot these novae clusters in XY and UMAP space. For this plotting, we switch back into R.

```{r}
#| label: novae-plots
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-summary: "R Code"

df <- py$adata$obs %>% select(cell_ID, minor_cell_type, major_cell_type, starts_with("novae_domains_"))
umap_coords <- py$adata$obsm['UMAP']
colnames(umap_coords) <- c("UMAP1", "UMAP2")
xy_coords <- py$adata$obsm['spatial_mm']
colnames(xy_coords) <- c("x_slide_mm", "y_slide_mm")
df <- cbind(df, xy_coords, umap_coords)

domain_names <- c()
for(i in c(1:20)){
  pick <- which(colnames(df)==paste0('novae_domains_', i))
  print(pick)
  domain_names <- c(domain_names, sort(unique(as.character(df[,pick]))))
}
domain_names <- unique(domain_names)

if(length(domain_names) <= 26){
domain_colors <- pals::alphabet2(length(domain_names))
} else{
  set.seed(2025)
  domain_colors <- sample(colors(distinct = T), length(domain_names))
}
names(domain_colors) <- domain_names
results_list[['novae_model_1_domain_names']] <- names(domain_colors)
results_list[['novae_model_1_domain_colors']] <- as.character(domain_colors)
saveRDS(results_list, results_list_file)


for(i in c(1:19)){
  p <- ggplot(data=df, 
              aes(x=x_slide_mm, y=y_slide_mm, color=.data[[paste0('novae_domains_', i)]])) + 
    geom_point(size=0.01, alpha=0.8) + 
    theme_bw() + 
    coord_fixed() + 
    scale_color_manual(values = domain_colors) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 5, alpha=1)))
  
  ggsave(filename = file.path(niche_dir, "Plots", paste0("xy_model_1_domain_", i, ".png")), p,
       width=16, height=16)
  
  p1 <- ggplot(data=df, 
              aes(x=UMAP1, y=UMAP2, color=.data[[paste0('novae_domains_', i)]])) + 
    geom_point(size=0.005, alpha=0.1) + 
    theme_bw() + 
    coord_fixed() + 
    scale_color_manual(values = domain_colors) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 5, alpha=1)))
  
  ggsave(filename = file.path(niche_dir, "Plots", paste0("umap_model_1_domain_", i, ".png")), p1,
       width=8, height=8)  

}

x_range <- range(df$x_slide_mm)
y_range <- range(df$y_slide_mm)
for(i in c(1:19)){
  pick <- which(colnames(df)==paste0("novae_domains_", i))
  i_domains <- as.character(unique(df[,pick]))
  for(j in i_domains){
    if(is.na(j)){
      next
    }
    dat <- df[df[,pick]==j,]
    p_x <- ggplot() + 
    geom_point(data = dat, size=0.005, alpha=0.3,
               aes(x=x_slide_mm, y=y_slide_mm), color="red") +
    theme_bw() + 
    coord_fixed() + 
    scale_x_continuous(limits=x_range) + 
    scale_y_continuous(limits=y_range)
    ggsave(filename=file.path(niche_dir, "Plots", paste0("xy_model_1_domain_level_", i, "_domain_", j, ".png")),
         plot=p_x, width=8, height=8, dpi=250) 
  }
}

# Save 9 domain assignments to a separate file for easy access.
novae_9 <- df$novae_domains_9
names(novae_9) <- row.names(df)
saveRDS(novae_9, file = paste0(niche_dir, "/Data/novae_domains_9_assignments.rds"))


```


We evaluated domains of various sizes, cutting off the hierarchy at levels leading up to at most 19 distinct domains. For this we visualize the spatial and umap positioning of each hierarchy level.

::: {.panel-tabset}

```{r}
#| output: asis
#| eval: true


files <- sortFiles(c(Sys.glob(file.path(niche_dir, "Plots", "xy_model_1_domain_[0-9].png")),
                     Sys.glob(file.path(niche_dir, "Plots", "xy_model_1_domain_[0-9][0-9].png"))), 5)
umap_files <- sortFiles(c(Sys.glob(file.path(niche_dir, "Plots", "umap_model_1_domain_[0-9].png")),
                          Sys.glob(file.path(niche_dir, "Plots", "umap_model_1_domain_[0-9][0-9].png"))), 5)

get_domain_number <- function(a_file){
  return(gsub('.png', '', strsplit(a_file, split='xy_model_1_domain_')[[1]][2]))
}
domains <- as.numeric(sapply(files, get_domain_number))

res <- purrr::map_chr(domains, \(i) {
    knitr::knit_child(text = c(
      "#### `r paste0('Domains: ', i)`",
      "",
      "",
      "```{r eval=TRUE}",
      "#| echo: false",

      "```{r eval=TRUE}",
      "#| echo: false",
      "#| fig-width: 10",
      "knitr::include_graphics(file.path(niche_dir, 'Plots', basename(umap_files[i])))",
      "```",
      "",
      ""
    ), envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE)
  })

cat(res, sep = '\n')

Based on spatial distribution and minor cell type composition, we assign each domain as a tumor core (TC) domain, interior stroma (IS), or exterior stroma (ES). 

```{r}
#| label: novae-domain9-names
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| code-summary: "R Code"

novae_9 <- readRDS(file = paste0(niche_dir, "/Data/novae_domains_9_assignments.rds"))

novae_9 <- dplyr::recode(
  novae_9,
  "D987" = "ES1",
  "D1003" = "ES2",
  "D1012" = "TC1",
  "D1013" = "TC2",
  "D976" = "TC3",
  "D1007" = "IS1",
  "D1008" = "IS2",
  "D1014" = "IS3",
  "D1011" = "IS4"
)

saveRDS(novae_9, file = paste0(niche_dir, "/Data/novae_domains_9_namedAssignments.rds"))

```

zooms = results_list$zoom_regions

# Read in polygons
polygons <- fread(paste0(objects_dir, "/FlatFiles/flatFiles/BreastCancer/BreastCancer-polygons.csv.gz"))
polygons$x_slide_mm <- polygons$x_global_px * 0.12028/1000
polygons$y_slide_mm <- polygons$y_global_px * 0.12028/1000

# Merge in novae domain
polygons <- merge(polygons, df[,c("cell_ID", "novae_9")], by.x = "cell", by.y = "cell_ID", all.y = T)

# Plot for each zoom region
for (zoom in zooms){
  
  
  idx <- which(
    polygons$x_slide_mm > zoom$xmin &
      polygons$x_slide_mm < zoom$xmax &
      polygons$y_slide_mm > zoom$ymin &
      polygons$y_slide_mm < zoom$ymax
  )
  
  scale_bar <- make_scale_bar_r(polygons[idx, c("x_slide_mm")], polygons[idx, "y_slide_mm"])
  
  ggplot(polygons[idx,],
         aes(x_slide_mm, y_slide_mm, group = cell)) +
    geom_polygon(aes(x_slide_mm, y_slide_mm, group = cell, fill = novae_9)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = domain_colors_9_named) +
    theme_void() +  
    coord_fixed() +  
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    scale_bar$bg + 
    scale_bar$rect + 
    scale_bar$label
  ggsave(paste0(niche_dir, "/Plots/", "xy_model_1_domain_9_colorsSelected_named_zoomed_", zoom$region, ".png"),
         width = 4, height = 4, units = "in", dpi = 400)
}

Plot top pathways per domain, using HieraType marker heatmap code.
```{r}
#| label: plot_top_pathways_per_domain
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: true
#| eval: false

# Read in pathway scores
pwd <- readRDS(file = paste0(pathway_dir, "/Data/cellsAUC_full.rds"))

if (!("seu.obj" %in% ls())){
  seu.obj <- readRDS(results_list$seurat_file_postCellTyping)
}

# Read in named novae domains
novae_9 <- readRDS(paste0(niche_dir, "/Data/novae_domains_9_namedAssignments.rds"))

# Extract metadata and add novae domains
df <- seu.obj@meta.data
df$novae_domain_9 <- novae_9[df$cell_ID]
if(all(df$cell_ID) == colnames(pwd)){
  
  ## Heatmap of pathways by domain
  pwfctbl <- 
    HieraType::clusterwise_foldchange_metrics(normed = pwd
                                              ,metadata = df[,c("novae_domain_9", "cell_ID")]
                                              ,cluster_column = "novae_domain_9")
  
  
  # Save it
  saveRDS(pwfctbl, file = paste0(niche_dir, "/Data/pwfctbl_novae9.rds"))
  
  # Remove NA cluster and 'reactome' from pathway names
  pwfctbl <- pwfctbl[!(is.na(pwfctbl$cluster)),]
  pwfctbl$gene <- gsub("REACTOME-", "", pwfctbl$gene)
  
  # Replace some pathway names with shorter abbreviations for better plotting
  pwfctbl$gene <- dplyr::recode(pwfctbl$gene,
                                "TP53-REGULATES-TRANSCRIPTION-OF-SEVERAL-ADDITIONAL-CELL-DEATH-GENES-WHOSE-SPECIFIC-ROLES-IN-P53-DEPENDENT-APOPTOSIS-REMAIN-UNCERTAIN" = "(*)TP53-REGULATED-CELL-DEATH",
                                "CROSS-PRESENTATION-OF-PARTICULATE-EXOGENOUS-ANTIGENS-PHAGOSOMES" = "(*)EXOGENOUS-ANTIGENS-PRESENTATION",
                                "NR1H2-NR1H3-REGULATE-GENE-EXPRESSION-LINKED-TO-LIPOGENESIS" = "(*)NR1H2-NR1H3-REGULATED-LIPOGENESIS",
                                "DEFECTIVE-CHST14-CAUSES-EDS-MUSCULOCONTRACTURAL-TYPE" = "(*)DEFECTIVE-CHST14-CAUSES-EDS")
  
  # Change pathway names to first letter capitalized
  pwfctbl$gene <- stringr::str_to_sentence(pwfctbl$gene)
  pwfctbl$gene <- gsub("-", " ", pwfctbl$gene)
  
  ## Plot it as a tile plot since fraction of cells doesn't have much meaning for a pathway
  # Extract features to use and order as in HieraType code
  fctable <- data.table::copy(pwfctbl)
  fctable[, `:=`(scaled_fold_change, fold_change/max(fold_change)), 
          by = gene]
  fctable[, `:=`(scaled_expr, cluster_expr/max(cluster_expr)), 
          by = gene]
  fctable[is.na(scaled_fold_change), `:=`(scaled_fold_change, 
                                          0)]
  fctable[is.na(scaled_expr), `:=`(scaled_expr, 0)]
  dmat <- data.table::dcast(fctable, gene ~ cluster, 
                            value.var = "scaled_fold_change")
  fc_mat <- as.matrix(dmat[, -c("gene"), with = FALSE])
  rownames(fc_mat) <- dmat[, gene]
  
  featsuse <- unique(c(fctable[order(-fold_change)][cluster_prop > 
                                                      0.05, head(.SD, 3), by = cluster][, 
                                                                                        unique(gene)]))
  
  suppressMessages(hmap <- ComplexHeatmap::Heatmap(fc_mat[featsuse, 
  ]))
  suppressMessages(grid::grid.grabExpr(hmap <- ComplexHeatmap::draw(hmap)))
  
  gene_order <- featsuse[ComplexHeatmap::row_order(hmap)]
  
  ct_order <- colnames(fc_mat)[ComplexHeatmap::column_order(hmap)]
  
  pd <- fctable[gene %in% featsuse]
  pd[, `:=`(gene, factor(gene, levels = gene_order))]
  pd[, `:=`(cluster, factor(cluster, levels = ct_order))]
  
  
  pd[, `:=`(rnk, rank(-fold_change)), by = gene]
  pd[, `:=`(gene, factor(gene, levels = pd[rnk == 1][order(cluster, 
                                                           -fold_change)][, unique(gene)]))]
  
  
  ggplot(as.data.frame(pd),
         aes(y = cluster, x = gene, fill = scaled_expr)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradientn(colors = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(9, "Blues"), 
                         name = "Scaled Pathway Score") +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, 
                                     size = 12),
          axis.title.x = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
          axis.title.y = element_blank()) +
    coord_flip()
  ggsave(filename = paste0(niche_dir, 
                           "/Plots/heatmap_pathways_by_domain_formatted.png"),
         height = 5, width = 8, units = "in", dpi = 300)
  
  
}
```
